name: status
title: Status
description: Where the game is, said once, in the middle of the scene: ready before a round, go as it starts, paused while it is held, complete when it has settled. Specimen 3b draws the four as one card with a fill, an ink and a size per state, and until this existed every host drew its own, which is four vocabularies for one fact. It is not a stat: there is no number, no max, no delta and no settlement, which is why StatKind has listed `status` since the beginning and drawn nothing for it. It carries `data-gs-stat="status"` so a HUD's existing selectors still find it and `data-gs-component="status"` so a test can tell it from the numbers. The card is a live region, so the change is announced rather than only drawn. Performs nothing: it does not start a round, run a countdown or decide that the game is over. Use `stat` for anything that is a number, and `timer` when the component must run the clock.

files.content:
'use client' import * as React from 'react' import { useStrings, type StringsOverrides } from './strings' // The component brings its own styles. Without this a `gamestage-ui add` installs a // working but completely unstyled Status, and `tsc --noEmit` passes on it, so the // gate cannot catch it. import './status.css' // The shared rule sets, so the theme's display face and its shadow reach the // word on the card. GSUI-118: the file shipped with the tokens and nothing // imported it, so the classes matched nothing in a real install. import './gamestage-primitives.css' /** * Status: where the game is, said once, in the middle of the scene. * * Specimen 3b draws four cards and calls them one object: READY before a round, * GO! as it starts, PAUSED while it is held and COMPLETE when it has settled. * Every round of every game passes through all four, and until this existed * every host drew its own, which is four vocabularies for one fact and four * places for the reduced-motion rule to be missed. * * It is not a stat. `stat` renders a number and this renders a state, which is * why `StatKind` has listed `status` since the beginning and drawn nothing for * it: there is no number to count up, no `max`, no delta and no settlement. It * carries `data-gs-stat="status"` so a HUD's existing selectors still find it, * and `data-gs-component="status"` so a test can tell it from the numbers. * * It performs nothing. It does not start a round, run a countdown or decide * that the game is over. The host owns the state; this draws it and reports * nothing back. * * `role="status"` because the change is the point. A player watching the scene * sees the card swap; a player using a screen reader gets nothing unless the * region announces itself, and "the round has started" is exactly the kind of * thing a polite live region is for. */ export type StatusValue = 'ready' | 'go' | 'paused' | 'complete' export interface StatusProps extends Omit, 'children'> { /** Per-instance vocabulary, merged over the provider. */ strings?: StringsOverrides /** Where the game is. Host-driven, always. */ value: StatusValue /** * The word on the card, when the game has its own. Defaults to the * vocabulary's word for the value, so a host that says nothing gets English * and a host with a provider gets whatever it supplied. */ label?: string } /** * The card that arrives pops, and only the one the drawing pops. * * Specimen 3b's note reads "READY→GO: motion.pop then motion.exit 300ms". The * pop belongs to GO!, which is the moment the round starts; READY is the card * already on screen when the player arrives. * * Nothing is keyed here, and that is the point. `stat` keys its value element * because the same motion has to replay for repeated changes of one number, * and a capability plays on mount. This card cannot go from `go` to `go`, so * the attribute going from absent to `pop` on a live element is enough: * motion.css's rule starts matching and gs-pop runs. * * Keying the root would have cost the announcement. `role="status"` is a live * region, and a screen reader announces a mutation inside an existing region; * a key change unmounts the region and inserts a populated one in its place, * which NVDA and JAWS read unreliably or not at all. The card would then have * been drawn correctly and silent, which is the state the role exists to * prevent. Reduced motion is motion.css's to honour and is not restated here. */ export function Status(props: StatusProps) { const { strings, value, label, className, ...rest } = props const copy = useStrings(strings) const word = label ?? copy[`status.${value}`] const going = value === 'go' return (
{/* Two bars before the word, the drawing's pause mark. Spans rather than an SVG: it is two rectangles, and a mark that is two rectangles does not earn a drawing in the shared glyph set. aria-hidden because the word beside it already says PAUSED, and a screen reader reading the mark as well would say it twice. */} {value === 'paused' ? ( ) : null} {word}
) }

docs: Pass `value` as one of ready, go, paused or complete; the host owns which. Pass `label` when the game has its own word for a state, or supply the whole vocabulary through StringsProvider. Place it at the centre of a `stage` layer: the card does not position itself.
